chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"Do not slaughter the sheep in front of another sheep, nor the large camel (or cow) while it is looking at its companion."
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on slaughtering animals in front of other animals?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on sacrifices, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (via the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali) establishes the principle of *ihsan* (excellence) in animal slaughter by preventing the visual trauma of witnessing a同类's death. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on minimizing animal suffering as a spiritual discipline, linking physical compassion to moral refinement. It serves as a foundational text for the ethical treatment of livestock in Islamic jurisprudence.
